newsitem.title: USA: Nasdaq, technology stocks suffer late retreat.
newsitem.headline: Nasdaq, technology stocks suffer late retreat.

text.p: Nasdaq shares staged a late retreat, with Blue Chip technology stocks becoming the biggest casualties, as stocks followed a decline in the bond market, traders said.

The Nasdaq Composite Index gained 1.56 points or 0.12 percent to an unofficial close of 1354.37, retreating from an earlier high of 1370.69. Gainers beat losers 2345 to 2013 on volume of 679 million shares.

The Dow industrials lost five points or 0.07 percent to close unofficially at 6656, after its 100-point rally crumbled. The long bond also slipped from earlier highs, gaining only 7/32 to yield 6.93 percent in late trading.

Traders said stocks began to lose steam as the bond market rally eased. The decline picked up speed after President Clinton said that his budget will contain a proposed homeowner capital gains exemption, but that a broader capital gains cut was not a priority, one trader said.

Technology stocks suffered the biggest wounds of the volatile session. 3Com Corp, the most active Nasdaq issue, pulled back from a high of 68-3/4 and dropped to 61-1/4, down 3-1/2. Microsoft Corp lost 1/2 to 95-5/8, after jumping to 98-3/4 earlier in the day.
